questions.prompt: What is Anthropic's "golden rule" of prompting?

options.text: If a colleague with minimal context would be confused by your prompt, Claude will be too
Always write prompts in all capital letters

questions.explanation: The guide's golden rule: show your prompt to a colleague with minimal context and ask them to follow it. If they'd be confused, Claude will be too.

questions.prompt: What makes few-shot examples effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: They're relevant to your real use case
They're diverse and cover edge cases

questions.explanation: Examples should be relevant, diverse, and structured in tags. Near-identical examples can make Claude copy accidental patterns.

questions.prompt: Labels like <instructions> and <context> that separate the parts of a prompt are called ____ tags.
questions.explanation: XML tags help Claude parse prompts that mix instructions, context, examples, and input.

questions.prompt: Which formatting instruction follows Anthropic's advice best?

options.text: Write your answer as smoothly flowing prose paragraphs.
No lists, no bold, no headings, no tables.

questions.explanation: Tell Claude what to do instead of what not to do. Describing the desired output works better than a list of prohibitions.

questions.prompt: For a long-document task, order the parts of the prompt as Anthropic recommends.

items.text: The long documents, wrapped in tags
An instruction to quote relevant passages before answering

questions.explanation: Put long documents at the top and your query at the end (Anthropic saw up to 30% better quality), and ask Claude to ground its answer in quotes first.

questions.prompt: Match each technique to what it does.

pairs.right: Lets Claude generalize from your reason
Keeps order and completeness when they matter

questions.explanation: Each technique targets a different weakness: reasons help generalization, roles focus expertise, examples steer format, and numbered steps enforce order.
